sentences.text: Criminal Original Petition has been filed  under section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, to call  for the records relating to charge sheet in CC No.776 of  2019 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate No.1, Madurai  and to quash the same.
For Petitioners : Mr.S.D.Ramalingam
For Respondent : Mr.B.Nambiselvan  Additional Public Prosecut  O R D E R
This criminal original petition has been filed seeking quashment of the case in CC No776 of 2019 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate No.1, Madurai.

2.The case of the prosecution in brief:-
The complainant namely the Food Safety Officer attached to Madurai Corporation,
Viswanathapuram filed a private complaint stating that on information on 17/09/2018 at about 11.30 am along with police team, he made search in Door No.17,
Othuvar Lane, Keela Chithrai Veethi, Madurai.
At that time the shop owner by name Barvin V.Jail was available.
They introduced themselves to the shop owner and made search with the consent of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis shop owner.

At that time, they found the following banned tobacco products:-
Ganesh 701 Tobacco Premium Product  28 pockets Ganesh 701 Tobacco Premium 21 pocket Shankar Chaap Tobacco 6 pockets Miraj Swadeshi Tobacco 25 pockets RMD PANMASALA 50 boxes M Scented Tobacco Gold  56 boxes 3.Samples were lifted as per the procedure.
Further process was undertaken as per the procedure and rules.
The shop owner was also informed about the sending of samples to the laboratory for examination.
Samples were sent to the laboratory by following proper procedure and rules.
A report was received from forensic analysis, on 29/11/2018.

In the above said report, it has been stated that it was unsafe under sections 3(1)(zz)(iii) & (V), 26(2)(i) & (V) of Food Safety and Standards Act and also the sale of chewable tobacco is Prohibited as per the Tamil Nadu Government Gazzette No.184,

4.Seeking quashment of the same, this petition has been filed on the sole ground that the tobacco products banning order was challenged in Writ Appeal No.2093 of 2018 and WP Nos.3076 and 3084 of 2019.

One of the writ petition No.3076 of 2019 was filed to quash the private complaint pending on the file of the Judicial Magistrate No.II, Ariyalur in CC No.129 of 2018 and another Writ Petition in WP No.3084 of 2019 was filed seeking quashment of the Government Order, vide Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary No.184 (No. 1418/2013/S8/FSSA), dated 23.05.2018.

sentences.text: 5.Heard both sides.
6.As mentioned above, this petition has been filed solely on the ground of order passed by the Division Bench of this court in WA No.2093 of 2018, dated 20/01/2023.
The GO No.184 (No.1418/2013/S8/FSSA), dated 23.05.2018 was the subject matter of WP No.3076 of 2019.

In the judgment reported in the case of The Designated Officer, The Food Safety & Drugs Control Department Vs. Jayavilas Tobacco (2023-1-L.W-639), elaborate discussion was made by the Division Bench of this court.

entities.text: Designated Officer, The Food Safety & Drugs Control Department Vs. Jayavilas Tobacco (2023-1-L.W-639)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
7.The above said writ petition was allowed by the single Judge.
Challenging the same, Food Safety Officer filed writ appeal before the Division Bench, as mentioned above.

After elaborate discussion,
the Hon'ble Division Bench of this court allowed WP Nos.3076 and 3084 of 2019, dated 20/01/2023.
8.The
following points were framed for consideration.

7.From the pleadings and   submissions of the counsel on e side, the following core issues arise in these proceedings before us:
(i)Whether the enactment of The Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (COTPA) by invoking the power under Article 52 of the Constitution of India would denude the parliament to enact any other law relating to Cigarettes and Tobacco Products. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (ii)Whether there is nay conflict between the COTPA and the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in relation to Tobacco products.

sentences.text: 3 (iii)whether COTPA a special enactment would prevail over the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, a subsequent General Law.
(iv)Whether Tobacco or Tobacco  Products would fall within the definition of food under Section 3(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

(v)Whether the provisions of Section 30(2)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 confer the power on the Commissioner, Food Safety to impose a total ban on the sale of Tobacco and Tobacco products by issuing successive notification year on year.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
9.Tobacco products with or without addiction will be the Food Products, as defined in section 3(g) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
But so far as the power of the Commissioner of Food Safety to impose the ban is concerned, it is concluded that no such power is available.
Issuance of successive ban orders is beyond the powers of the Director of Food Safety, on that ground, above said notification was quashed.
10.But against the judgment, Government of Tamil Nadu preferred SLP before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, wherein stay has been passed.
The ground on which, this petition has been filed is now become non-existing.
The petitioner can revive the petition at the appropriate time, if the trial is not completed within a period of six months, depending upon the SLP that was filed by the State.
11.So with the above said liberty, this criminal original petition stands dismissed.
But however, there shall be a direction to the trial court to expedite the trial process and complete the same within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis closed.
